Subject: CC
Description: An overview of the history of computers and programming. Famous historical figures and their impact in modern computing. Introduction to major topics in computer science such as artificial intelligence, high performance computing, cryptography, big data, cybersecurity, robotics, and more.
SLO1: Describe the history of Computing Science and list some of the important devices, innovations, and people that got us to where we are today.
SLO2: Relate Computing Science to a variety of other disciplines and describe how they are interconnected with each other.
SLO3: Apply and use Computing Science tools and techniques to solve real-world problems.
SLO4: Research and learn about new ideas and areas in Computing Science and share those ideas with others.
SLO5: Develop a personal understanding of how Computing Science affects their own life.
SLO6: Understand many different subject areas within Computing Science and how they are changing our understanding of the field.

Subject: CC
Description: Brief experience with computer programming concepts such as variables, data types, functions, conditionals, iteration, and collections.
SLO1: Identify and use variables in a computer program.
SLO2: Understand and use basic data types, such as integers, floating-point numbers, Booleans, and strings.
SLO3: Use conditional statements, including nested and chained conditional statements.
SLO4: Use both infinite and finite iteration constructs.
SLO5: Create and use functions.
SLO6: Create and use collections of data, such as lists and dictionaries.

Subject: CC
Description: The Internet, web browsers, and web-page-development technology: web-page design and implementation with Hypertext Markup Language (HTML), and CSS. Integration of program script into web pages. Introduction to graphics design, animation, and server utilization.
SLO1: Create valid HTML webpages using separation of concerns with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
SLO2: Use CSS rules to create engaging, effective, accessible, and responsive web page designs.
SLO3: Utilize HTML forms to submit data to a web API.
SLO4: Use JavaScript to dynamically modify the structure and appearance of a webpage.
SLO5: Employ AJAX/Fetch requests to interact with Web APIs.
SLO6: Think critically about web page design and apply solid web page design principles to their work.

Subject: CC
Description: Basic concepts in developing computer programs: program structure and syntax, primitive data types, variables, control flow, iteration, simple algorithms, debugging, and good software development practices. Introduction to object-oriented programming.

Subject: CC
Description: Exploration of data structures & related algorithms in computer programming. Basic concepts of complexity analysis. Object-oriented design concepts.

Subject: CC
Description: Advanced data structures and related algorithms. Formal software development methods and software engineering fundamentals. Introduction to requirements analysis processes that provide the specification of algorithmic requirements.
SLO1: Develop implementations of the string builder, tree, trie, binary tree, matrix graph, list graph, and priority queue data structures
SLO2: Develop implementations of algorithms for tree traversals, graph traversals, minimum spanning trees, and other core algorithms related to these data structures.
SLO3: Develop programs that convert data from the real world into representations that can be stored in a common data structure.

SLO5: Compare and contrast data structures based on their uses and performance characteristics.
SLO6: Compare and contrast common algorithms based on their uses and performance characteristics.
SLO7: Describe how to adapt real world data into common data structures.
SLO8: Describe how to use common algorithms to answer real world questions.

Subject: CC
Description: Advanced programming techniques and projects. Concepts from simulation and modeling, media applications, secure design, information management, parallelism, and networking. Software development methodologies, processes, and design patterns. Practical experience with professional communication and collaboration.
SLO1: Develop code following industry best-practices for code style and documentation.
SLO2: Develop and execute unit tests that adequately test code for bugs and errors.

SLO4: Make use of source code management tools to maintain and store a code base.

Subject: CC
Description: Administration of the Windows and Linux operating systems, including installation, configuration, distributed file systems, firewalls and security, shell scripting, and user account management. Introduction to managing cloud computing resources.
SLO1: Understand the major components of an enterprise level computer network and server system.
SLO2: Design and implement a simple enterprise level server system and network, as well as provision workstations on that network quickly and easily.
SLO3: Communicate information about enterprise systems clearly and effectively to users of all skill levels and interests.
SLO4: Develop ways to increase efficiency by automating tasks whenever possible using scripting and configuration management tools.
SLO5: Understand and describe security risks in any enterprise system and any ways that they can be mitigated.
SLO6: Show how to monitor enterprise systems for problems and use that information to locate and fix any issues within the system.
SLO7: Work with cloud technologies and describe how they can be integrated into an enterprise information technology setup.

Subject: CC
Description: Fundamental principles and best practices of web development, user interface design, web API design, advanced web interfaces, web development frameworks, single-page web applications, web standards and accessibility issues.

Subject: CC
Description: Introduction to concepts and techniques in database management. Overview of relational databases, NoSQL databases, and related topics. Database programming and use of databases in applications. Theory and architecture of database management systems (DBMS).

Subject: CC
Description: An introduction to data science and discovery from data: Data wrangling, feature engineering, feature selection, statistical inference, correlations, principal component analysis, classification, regression, novelty detection, clustering, cross-validation, bootstrapping, class profiling, multidimensional scaling, association rules, visualization, data science and society.
SLO1: Define and profile data science problems, and solve it using machine learning and data analytics tools.
SLO2: Understand and be able to apply basic machine learning and data analytic techniques.
SLO3: Identify machine learning and computing strategies to approach and solve problems using data.
SLO4: Understand discovery methods and their application to turn data into knowledge.
SLO5: Use statistical inference to explore data and determine the significance of discoveries.

Subject: CC
Long Title: Special Topics in Applied Computer Science
Description: Selected topics in applied computer science.

Subject: CC
Description: This course is a first step in preparing educators to teach computer science topics at the PreK-12 level. It provides content area knowledge including the historical context in which computing developed, an overview of the modern field of computing and its impacts on society. It also explores theories of computational thinking and learning, computer science education research, and the Kansas PreK-12 computer science standards.
SLO1: Describe the history of Computing Science and list some of the important devices, innovations, and people that got us to where we are today.
SLO2: Relate Computing Science to a variety of other disciplines and describe how they are interconnected with each other.
SLO3: Apply and use Computing Science tools and techniques to solve real-world problems.
SLO4: Research and learn about new ideas and areas in Computing Science and share those ideas with others.
SLO5: Develop a personal understanding of how Computing Science affects his or her own life.
SLO6: Understand many different subject areas within Computing Science and how they are changing our understanding of the field.
SLO7: Describe how current theories of learning apply to learning Computer Science and programming.
SLO8: Be able to articulate current findings in Computer Science Education Research.
SLO9: Describe the critical issues facing the field of computer science (and how these can be addressed by educators): Lack of diversity in the field; Ethical and cybersecurity concerns.

Subject: CC
Description: This course introduces PreK-12 educators to the ""Big ideas"" of programming - concept knowledge that is critical for developing and teaching programming skills. Students will learn to read simple program code, write short programs, and explore basic programming constructs such as conditional statements and iteration. Students will also explore basic programming concepts related to a particular discipline.
SLO1: Describe the basic syntax of a language.
SLO2: Create programs in a language that use variables and math operators to store and manipulate data.
SLO3: Create programs in a language that use functions, parameters, and returns to decompose programs into smaller parts.
SLO4: Create programs in a language that use conditional statements and iteration to change a program's control flow.
SLO5: Create programs in a language that use user inputs and print statements to interact with the user.
SLO6: Create programs in a language that use basic data structure such as lists and dictionaries.
SLO7: Relate their own experiences in learning programming to the learning theories discussed in CC 710.

Subject: CC
Description: The course introduces PreK-12 educators to computer programming using one of several programming languages. Interactive lessons and engaging projects reinforce new skills and concepts while exploring pedagogical strategies for teaching programming. This course covers the basic concepts of programming, from variables and control flow to functions, objects, and simple algorithms.
SLO1: Evaluate data requirements to create variables, use operators and call/create functions for: strings, integers, real numbers and Boolean values.
SLO2: Understand the creation and use of mono-typed Lists or Arrays and their common built in methods and attributes.
SLO3: Analyze and adapt string methods to split, join and extract sub-strings to solve problems.
SLO4: Understand how code written by them may throw exceptions; Understand how to create new exceptions; Understand and adapt exception handling structures.
SLO5: Understand how to create programs that read-from and write-to text files.
SLO6: Analyze and create conditional statement to control program execution.
SLO7: Analyze and create loops to control program execution.
SLO8: Analyze and adapt methods/function to control program execution; Remember to consider separation of concerns when creating methods.
SLO9: Understand how to create instance-based classes to include: public/private access of components; attributes, properties and methods; inheritance.
SLO10: Understand how to adapt Boolean equations to common natural language problem statements.
SLO11: Understand how to adapt class APIs to incorporate objects in solutions.
SLO12: Analyze medium-to-low-level designs expressed as text-based program requirements to create programs including: UML Class diagrams, flow charts and pseudo code.
SLO13: Create terminal or console based programs.
SLO14: Articulate the differences between novice and expert programmers.
SLO15: Describe how students move from novice to expert in programming skills.
SLO16: Write original lesson plans utilizing pedagogical methodologies specific to Computer Science Education.

Subject: CC
Long Title: Data Structures and Algorithms for Educators I
Description: This course provides PreK-12 educators the content knowledge necessary for teaching simple data structures such as sets, lists, stacks, queues, and maps. Students learn how to create data structures and the algorithms to work with them. Students are introduced to algorithm analysis to determine the efficiency of algorithms. It also addresses strategies for teaching these concepts to a diverse audience.
SLO1: Use preconditions, postconditions, and invariants to describe how a function works.
SLO2: Write a function that meets a set of given preconditions, postconditions, and invariants.
SLO3: Describe different types of data structures and algorithmic techniques.
SLO4: Develop implementations of the stack, queue, linked list, set, and hash table data structure.
SLO5: Develop implementations of standard searching and sorting algorithms.
SLO6: Implement recursive functions and compare and contrast them with iterative implementations.
SLO7: Compare and contrast data structures based on their uses and performance characteristics.
SLO8: Compare and contrast common algorithms based on their uses and performance characteristics.
SLO9: Use standard library implementations of the various data structures covered in this class.
SLO10: Create appropriate lesson plans to introduce these concepts to students, relating back to a teacher's area of interest.

Subject: CC
Long Title: Data Structures and Algorithms for Educators II
Description: This course provides PreK-12 educators the content knowledge necessary for teaching advanced data structures, such as trees, graphs, and heaps, along with pedagogical approaches for teaching the associated concepts and skills. Several new algorithms using these data structures are covered. Students also learn software development methods and software engineering fundamentals and use those skills to develop projects of increasing size and scope effectively.
SLO1: Develop implementations of the string builder, tree, trie, binary tree, matrix graph, list graph, and priority queue data structures
SLO2: Develop implementations of algorithms for tree traversals, graph traversals, minimum spanning trees, and other core algorithms related to these data structures.
SLO3: Develop programs that convert data from the real world into representations that can be stored in a common data structure.
SLO4: Use real world data stored in a data structure to answer a question using common algorithms for the data structure.
SLO5: Compare and contrast data structures based on their uses and performance characteristics.
SLO6: Compare and contrast common algorithms based on their uses and performance characteristics.
SLO7: Describe how to adapt real world data into common data structures.
SLO8: Describe how to use common algorithms to answer real world questions.
SLO9: Create appropriate lesson plans to introduce these concepts to students, relating back to a teacher's area of interest.

Subject: CC
Description: This course helps PreK-12 educators gain experience writing programs using a variety of advanced programming techniques including object-oriented programming, inheritance, and events. It also introduces software development methodologies, processes, and design patterns, along with pedagogical strategies to teach them. It also emphasizes collaboration skills and tools used by professional programmers.
SLO1: Develop code following industry best-practices for code style and documentation.
SLO2: Develop and execute unit tests that adequately test code for bugs and errors.
SLO3: Make use of tools to determine the code coverage of a set of unit tests.
SLO4: Make use of source code management tools to maintain and store a code base.
SLO5: Create a class library following the object-oriented paradigm that makes effective use of inheritance and polymorphism where appropriate.
SLO6: Develop a GUI for a given program that uses event-driven programming to respond to GUI events and manipulate underlying data models.
SLO7: Apply common software development methodologies, processes and design patterns to create software that performs a desired task or solves a problem.
SLO8: Communicate information about their code effectively with various audiences.
SLO9: Describe how project-based learning can be integrated into programming courses.
SLO10: Be prepared to mentor students on open-ended programming projects.

Subject: CC
Description: Topics in Computing Education for PreK-12 educators. Topics will be determined by faculty.
SLO1: Research a relevant topic in computing education.
SLO2: Communicate clearly and effectively with a wide range of audiences about a relevant topic in computing education.
SLO3: Demonstrate how a relevant topic in computing education can be used to inform teaching practices and/or curriculum design.

Subject: CIS
Description: Presentation of professional problems and practices by students, faculty, and industry professionals associated with computing and information sciences.

Subject: CIS
Description: Presentation of professional problems and practices by students, faculty, and professionals associated with computing science.

Subject: CIS
Description: A survey of the discipline of Computing Science and its interaction with other disciplines, incorporating historical development, theories, and tools of Computing Science (algorithm design and programming). Topics include: mechanical and digital computers, computational thinking, security, simulation, data science, web technologies, and more. Students will be able to explore real-world problems within computer science and research current topics.
SLO1: Describe the history of Computing Science and list some of the important devices, innovations, and people that got us to where we are today.
SLO2: Relate Computing Science to a variety of other disciplines and describe how they are interconnected with each other.
SLO3: Apply and use Computing Science tools and techniques to solve real-world problems.
SLO4: Research and learn about new ideas and areas in Computing Science and share those ideas with others, all without direct guidance.
SLO5: Develop a personal understanding of how Computing Science affects their own life.
SLO6: Understand many different subject areas within Computing Science and how they are changing our understanding of the field.

Subject: CIS
Description: An introduction to programming by exploring core concepts such as variables, conditionals, iteration, basic data structures,  functions, and classes. Hands-on activities to learn and apply concepts to real-world problems and ideas. Students will gain a solid foundation in programming, setting the stage for further study and professional use.
SLO1: Understand the basics of computer programming and the significance of Python in the tech world.
SLO2: Set up a Python development environment.
SLO3: Write, debug, and execute Python programs.
SLO4: Utilize Python’s built-in functions, libraries, and modules.
SLO5: Understand and apply the basic structures of programming, including variables, data types, operators, control structures, loops, and functions.
SLO6: Engage with basic object-oriented programming concepts like classes and objects.
SLO7: Create basic real-world applications using Python.

Subject: CIS
Description: Participation in various professional development activities at an international university.

Subject: CIS
Long Title: Undergraduate Seminar in Computing and Information Science
Description: Topics of special interest in computing and information sciences.

Subject: CIS
Description: Principles of algorithm design and their application to procedural programming: state, control structures, methods. Patterns of conditional and iterative control structure.  Program testing. Introduction to arrays, classes, and objects.  Programming projects.
SLO1: Explain and apply core object-oriented programs principles, including subclasses, encapsulation, inheritance, and abstraction.
SLO2: Develop robust programs by implementing error-handling techniques, including exception handling, in object-oriented programs.
SLO3: Enumerate the differences between imperative and object-oriented programming paradigms.
SLO4: Compose a class through design, implementation, and testing to meet behavioral requirements.
SLO5: Demonstrate knowledge and use of object-oriented programming, collection classes, and iterators and apply them effectively in problem-solving.
SLO6: Use structured problem-solving techniques to decompose complex problems and develop effective, efficient solutions through object-oriented programming principles.

Subject: CIS
Description: Application of computers to engineering problems. Abstraction and problem solving; algorithms; control structures; input/output; functions; arrays and array processing.

Subject: CIS
Description: A study of common data and program structures together with associated algorithms. Topics include interfaces, design patterns, arrays, stacks, queues, lists, trees, hash tables, recursion, binary search, and tree traversals. Experience with both use and implementation of these structures and algorithms using a modern programming language. Discussion of tradeoffs involving performance and software maintainability.

Subject: CIS
Description: Logical formalisms used to model and reason about computer systems. Propositional and predicate logic, syntax, semantics, and proof theory; soundness and completeness issues. Mathematical induction. Program verification: invariants and program logics.
SLO1: Write and interpret claims in propositional and predicate logic
SLO2: Formally reason about logical arguments using truth tables and natural deduction
SLO3: Prove arguments using mathematical induction and other techniques
SLO4: Write and interpret specifications and invariants describing program behavior
SLO5: Use formal logic to reason about program correctness

Subject: CIS
Description: Fundamentals of programming in C.

Subject: CIS
Description: Knowledge and skills needed to administer and defend computer networks and systems. Topics include the basics of computer networks, intelligence gathering, network scanning and sniffing, password security and cracking, vulnerability exploitation, distributed denial of service, logging and auditing, and wireless network security and cracking. Practice using an isolated computing network.

Subject: CIS
Description: Honors Seminar in Computer Science

Subject: CIS
Description: A study of concepts and techniques used to produce quality software programs. Object-oriented concepts, models, execution environments, design and testing techniques. Extensive application of these concepts and techniques to the development of non-trivial software programs.

Subject: CIS
Long Title: Ethics and Conduct for Computing Professionals
Description: A study of the ethical issues raised by computing technologies and the impact on society. Exploration of how one might justify actions in regard to ethical dilemmas within the fields of technology, computer science, information security, and artificial intelligence. Other topics include an examination of terminology used, Profession Codes of Conduct for computer science professionals, ethics of software development, and ethical issues relating to privacy and intellectual property in cyberspace.
SLO1: Encourage students to consider how their knowledge and actions within their profession affect others
SLO2: Expose students to both the ethical and legal issues that are a part of the information technology arena and their effects on business, industry, policy, and society
SLO3: Acquaint students with the ethical responsibilities and codes of conduct expected in the profession
SLO4: Improve students’ ability to think critically and defend decisions logically regarding ethical and moral issues in computing
SLO5: Give students a greater appreciation for alternate points of view
SLO6: Provide students with a minimal theoretical background essential for their understanding of the role that personal values and ethics play in decision-making
SLO7: Recognize professional responsibilities and make informed judgments based on legal principles (ABET 4)
SLO8: Recognize professional responsibilities and make informed judgments based on ethical principles (ABET 4)
SLO9: Evaluate an AI system for issues related to bias, fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy, and responsible use. (ABET 4)

Subject: CIS
Description: Introduction to modern computer architectures: register transfer abstraction, addressing modes, basic operations (data transfer, arithmetic/logic, and control operations). Basic Operating System concepts and operations. Understanding relationships of higher-level language constructs to corresponding assembly instruction sequences generated by compilers. Introduction to interrupts and low-level I/O operations.

Description: Current topics in computer science.

Description: Open to students pursuing undergraduate research projects.

Subject: CIS
Description: Principles and patterns for design and structure of software, development of object-oriented models, examples of software architecture.

Subject: CIS
Description: History, programming language concepts including type, scope and extent, abstraction mechanisms and control; programming paradigms, including one or more of logic, functional, and object-oriented programming, and programming languages supporting the selected paradigms; interpreters, compilers and virtual machines for the selected languages; storage management and garbage collection; type checking and type inference.

Subject: CIS
Description: Operating systems concepts, services, and implementation: interrupt processing, processes, concurrency, deadlocks, resource scheduling and system structure; resource management: real and virtual storage, input/output systems, disk scheduling and file systems; design and construction of concurrent programs.

Subject: CIS
Description: Introduction to basic data structures such as stacks, queues, lists, and priority queues, and algorithmic techniques for sorting, searching and hashing. Emphasis on modularity and reuse. Introduction to the concept of object-oriented design and interface specifications.

Subject: CIS
Description: Introduction to concurrent programming techniques based on message passing primitives (send/receive) and shared memory (semaphore based P/V operations and monitor-based wait/signal operations).

Subject: CIS
Description: Basic inter-process communication and network programming concepts including client-server and peer-to-peer, communication protocol use and specification, reliable and secure communication, and network applications including web technologies, electronic mail, and file transfer with a focus on application and implementation.

Subject: CIS
Description: Fundamental principles and best practices of web development, user interface design, web API design, advanced web interfaces, web development frameworks, single-page web applications, web standards and accessibility issues.

Subject: CIS
Description: Administration of the Linux operating system, including installation, configuration, distributed file systems, firewalls and security, shell scripting, and user account management.
SLO1: Understand the major components of an enterprise level computer network and server system.
SLO2: Design and implement a simple enterprise level server system and network, as well as provision workstations on that network quickly and easily.
SLO3: Communicate information about enterprise systems clearly and effectively to users of all skill levels and interests.
SLO4: Develop ways to increase efficiency by automating tasks whenever possible using scripting and configuration management tools.
SLO5: Understand and describe security risks in any enterprise system and any ways that they can be mitigated.
SLO6: Show how to monitor enterprise systems for problems and use that information to locate and fix any issues within the system.
SLO7: Work with cloud technologies and describe how they can be integrated into an enterprise information technology setup.

Subject: CIS
Description: Fundamental background in intelligent systems for undergraduate students. Intelligent agents, problem-solving, uninformed and informed (heuristic) search, game tree search, foundations of knowledge representation and reasoning using logic and probability, and a first introduction to planning and machine learning. AI topics include the problem areas of natural language processing (NLP) and perception and methodologies such as artificial neural networks and genetic and evolutionary computation. Applications to practical design and development of intelligent systems will be emphasized, leading to individual projects on current topics and applications in AI.

Subject: CIS
Long Title: Introduction to Programming Techniques for Data Science and Analytics
Description: Introduction to programming techniques for working with big data. Survey of programming concepts that underlie the MapReduce architecture, their implementation, and specific tools for data integration and data transformation. Basic databases and query processing in the context of real-world problems.

Subject: CIS
Description: Foundations of deep learning, with focus on different types of modern neural network architectures (such as convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and transformers). Regularization and optimization in the context of deep learning. Frameworks and tools for building and training deep neural networks.

Subject: CIS
Description: Introduction to the foundations of data science and data analytics. Computer science concepts used for making discoveries in data. Data wrangling, feature engineering, classification, regression, clustering, outlier detection, societal aspects of data science, and more. Analysis of real-word data.
SLO1: Define and profile data science problems, and solve it using machine learning and data analytics tools.
SLO2: Understand and be able to apply basic machine learning and data analytic techniques.
SLO3: Identify machine learning and computing strategies to approach and solve problems using data.
SLO4: Understand discovery methods and their application to turn data into knowledge.
SLO5: Use statistical inference to explore data and determine the significance of discoveries.

Subject: CIS
Description: Introduction to computer graphics for undergraduate students. Mathematical foundations (e.g., linear, affine, and projective transformations) and fundamental topics in realistic rendering: view normalization, clipping and culling, scan conversion of lines and polygons, shading and illumination, texture mapping, user interfaces, picking, and collision handling. Intermediate topics include shaders, procedural textures, particle systems, basics of animation, fractals, color theory, and ray tracing.

Subject: CIS
Description: Theory and applications of computer vision. Introduction to computer vision, introduction to image formation,

Subject: CIS
Description: Advanced concepts and practicum in object-oriented analysis, modeling, design, implementation, testing, and use of CASE tools; relationships among structural, static, and dynamic models; relationship among conceptual, system, and implementation models.

Subject: CIS
Long Title: Fundamentals of Computer and Information Security
Description: An introduction to computer and information security, including common attack techniques, application of cryptography in security, authentication and authorization, network security, enterprise network defense, web security, and analysis of design flaws that render a system vulnerable. Course projects provide hands-on experience on both the defense and offense aspects in cyberspace.

Subject: CIS
Description: Introduction to the fundamentals of cryptography, including mathematical background, classical ciphers, public key encryption, block and stream ciphers, cryptographic hash functions, digital signatures, common attacks, and basic security protocols.

Subject: CIS
Description: Concepts, approaches, and techniques in database management. Representation of information as data, data storage techniques, foundations of logical data models, data retrieval, database design, transaction management, integrity and security.

Subject: CIS
Long Title: Introduction to Data Science in Practice
Description: The development and implementation of computer science solutions to practical data science problems in science and industry. Implementing computer programs and applying computational tools to turn real-world data into knowledge and solve real-world data science problems. Includes a substantial capstone component.

Subject: CIS
Description: Formal languages, automata, regular expressions, grammars, introduction to computability theory. Reading and writing informal mathematical proofs pertaining to these topics.

Subject: CIS
Description: An introduction to mathematical analysis of time- and space-complexity of algorithms, including worst-case, average-case, and amortized complexity. An examination of various algorithmic designs, such as greedy algorithms, divide-and-conquer algorithms, and dynamic programming algorithms. Techniques for proving correctness of algorithms.

Subject: CIS
Description: Fundamental principles of programming games. Foundational game algorithms and data structures. Two-dimensional graphics and game world simulation. Development for multiple platforms. Utilization of game programming libraries. Design of multiple games incorporating topics covered.

Subject: CIS
Description: Current practices of game engine development. The game engine as a soft real-time multi-agent simulation.  Three-dimensional graphics and animation techniques, scene management, physics simulation, event systems, resource management, and network game architectures.  Design and prototyping of a general use game engine.

Description: Selected topics in computer science.

Description: Informal and axiomatic set theory, propositional and predicate logic, proof techniques.

Description: Relationship between C/C++ constructs and corresponding assembly code generated by compilers. Introduction to special techniques used to implement micro-controllers, such as initialization of programmable CPU modules/peripheral devices, techniques to link assembly and C/C++ codes, producing ROM-able code, and EPROM burning/Flash programming.

Subject: CIS
Description: Basic real-time operating systems concepts and services; interrupt processing; process and thread models; real-time software architectures and development environments. Detailed study of design and implementation of real-time applications using real-time operating systems.

Subject: CIS
Description: Architecture, design, modeling, implementation, and verification of concurrent, parallel, and distributed software; aspects such as real-time programming, parallel simulation; fault-tolerant programming; grid computing, embedded systems control.

Description: Introduction to the applications of artificial intelligence concepts to solving knowledge-dependent tasks. Review of knowledge-representation ideas. Survey of expert system design. Introduction to existing knowledge-based tools available on personal computers. Development of an intelligent system.

Description: Devices and software for graphics display and user interaction, development of software for direct graphic manipulation applications.

Subject: CIS
Description: Survey of software testing methodologies; evaluation of software testing strategies; experience in a variety of software testing practices.

Subject: CIS
Description: Current practices of software development, requirements, design, prototyping, measures and evaluations. Specification, design, and prototyping of a software system.

Description: The first semester of a two-semester capstone course. Current practices of software development, requirements, design, prototyping, measures and evaluation. Specification, design, and prototyping of a software system.

Description: Continuation of CIS 642. Final implementation, integration, and testing of a software system. Introduction to configuration management, project management, and software maintenance.

SLO5: Function effectively as a member or leader of a team engaged in software engineering activities.

Subject: CIS
Description: Survey of current development environments and/or an in-depth study of one development environment.

Subject: CIS
Long Title: Security and Reliability of Computing Systems
Description: Fundamentals of security and reliability of computing systems from both hardware and software perspectives. Topics include symmetric and asymmetric cryptography, artificial intelligence (AI) safety and security, selected topics from hardware-based security, introduction to reliability and fault tolerance, hardware fault tolerance, and software fault tolerance.

Subject: CIS
Description: The department will suggest various design or implementation projects for individuals or groups in areas such as translators, interpreters, microprogramming, minicomputer operating systems, graphics, numerical software, etc.

Subject: CIS
Description: Programming language concepts, including typing, scoping, abstraction and exceptions; programming paradigms, including one or more of logic, functional, object-oriented and concurrent programming, and programming languages supporting the selected paradigms; introduction to programming language semantics; programming language design; development environments.

Subject: CIS
Description: Compiler construction: language specification, finite-state scanners, LL parsing, abstract syntax, symbol tables and type checking, code generation for virtual machines, and introductory static analysis.
SLO1: Explain the structure of a compiler and the role of each phase, from lexical and syntactic analysis through code generation.
SLO2: Apply formal language theory to specify languages with regular expressions and context-free grammars, and construct parsing tables.
SLO3: Design and implement scanners and parsers using generators, construct abstract syntax representations, and implement semantic analysis for scoping and type checking.
SLO4: Implement code generation for an abstract machine, and apply basic optimizations and dataflow analyses.
SLO5: Extend and evaluate a large existing compiler to meet given language requirements.

Subject: CIS
Description: Process synchronization and communication, distributed programming primitives, transactions and concurrency control, distributed scheduling, distributed storage, deadlock, security.

Subject: CIS
Description: The design of hard real-time embedded systems, including language and operating system support, scheduling, schedulability analysis, fault tolerance, and design tools.

Subject: CIS
Description: Structure and functions of modern operating systems. Emphasis on reading and modifying the source code of a working operating system. This includes memory management, input/output, process management, file systems, and network interconnection software construction.

Subject: CIS
Description: Network algorithms; routing and congestion control; protocol engineering; protocol decomposition, specification and verification, synthesis; protocols for high speed networks; parallel implementations, light-weight protocols.

Subject: CIS
Description: An advanced course on the technologies that make up the World Wide Web. WWW site designs and analysis, WWW software architecture, server-side technologies, dynamic executable scheduling, digital libraries, WWW security.

Subject: CIS
Description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts and techniques of AI: problem solving, search and planning, knowledge representation and qualitative reasoning, expert systems, natural language processing and cognitive modeling, computer vision, and machine learning.

Subject: CIS
Long Title: Programming Techniques for Data Science and Analytics
Description: Intermediate programming techniques for data science. Survey of programming concepts that underlie MapReduce, Apache Hadoop, and Spark, along with related tools. NoSQL, search tools, graph databases, and visualization presented in the context of real-world problems involving data integration and transformation.

Subject: CIS
Description: Theory and methodology of inductive learning, including decision trees, artificial neural networks, probabilistic and instance-based learning, and inductive logic programming; unsupervised and reinforcement learning, bagging and boosting; genetic algorithms and genetic programming; and applications to data mining.

Subject: CIS
Description: Methods used for making discoveries in complex data and turning data into knowledge. Handling big data and ""small data"", feature engineering, convolutions, classification, regression, using clustering for discovery, novelty detection, statistical inference, research design, prescriptive analytics, and more. Using standard software packages and libraries for preparing and analyzing data, implementing supervised machine learning, and visualization.
SLO1: Define and profile data science problems, and solve it using machine learning and data analytics tools.
SLO2: Understand and be able to apply basic machine learning and data analytic techniques.
SLO3: Identify machine learning and computing strategies to approach and solve problems using data.
SLO4: Understand discovery methods and their application to turn data into knowledge.
SLO5: Use statistical inference to explore data and determine the significance of discoveries.

Subject: CIS
Description: A problem solving approach to understanding genomics and bioinformatics. Practical use of databases and web-based tools used to study biological problems. Introduction to the algorithms behind these tools.

Subject: CIS
Description: Topics in computer representation and display of images and graphic interaction.

Subject: CIS
Description: Theory and applications of computer vision. Introduction to computer vision, introduction to image formation, binary image processing, image enhancement and ltering, computational photography, geometric transforms, image features, image recognition, video analysis, deep learning-based computer vision, convolutional neural networks, and other selective topics on computer vision.

Subject: CIS
Description: Software life cycle, requirements, specifications, design, validation, measures, and maintenance.

Subject: CIS
Description: Advanced concepts and practicum in object-oriented analysis, modeling, design, implementation, testing, and use of CASE tools; relationships among structural, static, and dynamic models; relationship among conceptual, system, and implementation models.

Subject: CIS
Description: Measurement theory; development, validation and use of software measures; software measures in the life cycle, including cost estimation, design measures, software complexity and software reliability.

Subject: CIS
Description: Topics related to the management of software, including organization, project planning, process models, life cycle models, TQM, software quality assurance, cost estimation, configuration management.

Subject: CIS
Description: Fundamentals of quantitative design of computer architectures, memory hierarchy design, instruction-level parallelism, data-level parallelism, thread-level parallelism, parallel programming, parallel performance analysis, and warehouse-scale computers.

Subject: CIS
Description: A comprehensive coverage of computer and information security. Basic cryptography, access control, authentication, authorization, network security, software security, and social aspects of security. The lectures discuss when and where things can go wrong and how design flaws in a system can be exploited to compromise security. Common attack techniques are introduced, and students have the opportunity to work on course projects that cover both the defense and offense aspects in cyberspace.

Subject: CIS
Description: Fundamentals of cryptography, including mathematical background, classical ciphers, public key encryption, block and stream ciphers, cryptographic hash functions, digital signatures, common attacks, and basic network security.

Subject: CIS
Description: In-depth coverage of advanced theoretical and practical security techniques with emphasis on construction of new systems and auditing and repair of existing security-critical systems using rigorous design, risk analysis, and engineering methods and application of state-of-art theoretical tools.

Subject: CIS
Description: Data models and languages, hierarchical, network, relational systems; implementation and operational requirements; programming projects using data base management systems.

Subject: CIS
Description: Characteristics of information work; modeling systems for characterizing aspects of office environment; form-based systems; office automation and description languages, ergonomics, local area networks and tools used in the automation of offices.

Subject: CIS
Description: Conceptual, logical, physical, and user interface design for database management systems.

Subject: CIS
Description: Regular languages, finite automata, context-free languages, pushdown automata, context-sensitive languages, linear bounded automata, recursively enumerable languages, Turing machines.

Subject: CIS
Description: Formal specification of software at the abstract, architecture, and code levels; verification and validation through automated analysis, deductive reasoning, and testing.
SLO1: Apply set theory, relations, and logic to build abstract formal specifications that separate what a system must do from how.
SLO2: Analyze abstract specifications automatically to validate them against intended requirements, using counterexamples to revise them and to assess model refinements.
SLO3: Design system architectures with contract specifications for components and programs, and generate implementation infrastructure from architecture models.
SLO4: Evaluate implementations against their contracts, verifying correctness by deductive reasoning with inductive invariants and finding violations through systematic testing.

Subject: CIS
Description: Study and application of techniques and procedures used in the analysis of algorithms including the worst and average cases of both time and space. Study of the P and NP classes.

Description: Topics in Computer Science

Subject: CIS
Description: Advanced translator construction: compiler generators, semantic analysis, code generation for virtual machines, code optimization, and static program analysis using dataflow frameworks. Design and implementation of a substantial translator or program-analysis project.
SLO1: Design and implement language front ends from grammar specifications using compiler generators, including semantic analysis such as scoping and type checking.
SLO2: Implement code generation for a run-time model of program execution (activation records, operand stack, heap).
SLO3: Apply the monotone framework to formulate and solve classic dataflow problems, and use the results to justify meaning-preserving optimizations.
SLO4: Design, implement, and evaluate a substantial translator or program-analysis extension as a final project.

Subject: CIS
Description: Introduction of formal semantics description methods for programming languages; comparison of operational, denotational, algebraic, and axiomatic methods; analysis of relationship of formal semantics definitions to computer implementation.

Subject: CIS
Description: Selected topics; constraint logic programming, deductive databases, concurrent logic programming, object-oriented logic programming, mathematical theory of logic programming specification and transformation of logic programs.

Subject: CIS
Long Title: Topics in Theory of Asychronous Systems
Description: Safety and liveness properties, synchronous and asynchronous message passing systems, virtual circuit and datagram communication, process failure, concepts of composition and superimposition, temporal logic, reachability analysis, theory of concurrency control, atomic commitment, replica control.

Subject: CIS
Description: Models of distributed computation, events and global states, failure semantics, communication abstractions, synchronization in distributed programs; distributed algorithms: election, termination and deadlock detection, broadcast programming and algorithms.

Subject: CIS
Description: Basic concepts of protocol design, specification languages and formal description techniques, safety and liveness properties, protocol validation, protocol synthesis, protocol translation and conformance testing.

Subject: CIS
Description: Advanced techniques and new ideas in artificial intelligence. Includes applications and case studies of artificial intelligence in action.

Subject: CIS
Description: Foundations of deep learning, with focus on different types of modern neural network architectures (such as convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and transformers). Regularization and optimization in the context of deep learning. Frameworks and tools for building and training deep neural networks.

Subject: CIS
Long Title: Knowledge Representation for the Semantic Web
Description: Knowledge representation languages for data sharing and integration, in particular the W3C Semantic Web standards RDF, OWL and SPARQL; state of the art knowledge graph and knowledge graph schema modeling process; ontology design patterns; modular ontology engineering.

Subject: CIS
Description: Theory and practice of search engines for retrieving textual information; basic and advanced topics, with emphasis on newer technologies that go beyond simple keyword search; the use of MapReduce framework to process large collections of documents.

Subject: CIS
Description: The course will cover some of the most important machine learning algorithms (including semi-supervised and transfer learning algorithms) and their applications to bioinformatics.

Subject: CIS
Long Title: Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence: Deep Learning and Knowledge Representation
Description: State of the art in combining deep learning with symbolic artificial intelligence approaches based on the newest research publications on the topic.

Subject: CIS
Description: State of the art in knowledge graph based data management and applications; based on the newest research publications on the topic.

Subject: CIS
Description: Practical techniques for verifying and validating software including formal verification, software testing, reliability measurement and modeling.

Subject: CIS
Description: Review of formal specification languages; architecture of concurrent and reactive systems; specification methods including: Z, Petri nets, temporal logic, state transition models; development and evaluation of system specifications; verification structures including layered systems, serialization, and predicate automata.

Subject: CIS
Description: Analysis, design, and implementation of large, complex, distributed, and adaptive software systems using agent-oriented paradigm. Will survey various modeling languages and agent-oriented methodologies.

Subject: CIS
Description: Techniques for developing high assurance (safety critical, security critical, or mission-critical in nature) systems. Topics include writing requirements for safety-critical systems, formal architecture definition, risk management techniques including various forms of hazard analysis, safety systems, and verification and validation.
SLO1: Describe key elements of a development process for critical systems including concepts of risk management, verification, validation, assurance.
SLO2: Understand and explain the utility of model-driven development for embedded systems
SLO3: Be able to use standardized system modeling languages like AADL and/or SysMLv2 to specify the software architecture of a simple real-time embedded system
SLO4: Be able to use a language appropriate for safety-critical systems (e.g. SPARK Ada, Rust) to implement the application logic for a simple real-time embedded system
SLO5: Be able to use testing technologies and coverage assessment to argue that a component of a safety-critical system satisfies its requirements.
SLO6: Be able to use code-level formal verification techniques to demonstrate that a component of a safety-critical system satisfies its requirements.
SLO7: Be able to explain the role of safety standards in helping provide trust in safety-critical and security-critical devices such as medical devices, autonomous vehicles, civilian aircraft

Description: Advanced topics in database design and maintenance including performance monitoring, query optimization and tuning in centralized and distributed data systems.
